extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news organizations, journalism startups, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: The 'About the Lab' page for the Nieman Journalism Lab describing the Lab's mission, staff, licensing/copyright terms, fellowship deadlines, and invitations for reader contributions. It explains editorial focus and reuse rules for the site's content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License (reuse conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: All content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are free to translate, transform, reprint, or otherwise reuse our content, as long as (a) you are not using it for commercial purposes and (b) you attribute it to the Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the work’s author, preferably with a link back to the original content. Examples given: translate the entire site into Portuguese; redistribute some posts to students in a college course; use the Twitter feed as lyrics in a song. For any other use, contact the Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is © the President and Fellows of Harvard College or the content’s original author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site uses 'Some rights reserved' and clarifies that reuses beyond the Creative Commons noncommercial attribution terms should be arranged by contacting the Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowship application deadlines (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual deadline to apply for a fellowship is December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the formal, recurring deadline schedule for Nieman Fellowship applicants; applicants should plan submissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial focus / selection priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab aims to 'highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail,' to 'find good ideas for others to steal,' and to 'help reporters and editors adjust to their online labors' as well as help traditional news organizations survive and assist startups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames what the Lab chooses to cover and promotes content that showcases innovation in journalism, lessons about success and failure, replicable ideas, and practical help for practitioners; the site also solicits reader contributions and positions the Lab as a collaborative exchange of ideas.
